correctness.rationale: Each published edge vertex has three unit-magnitude coordinates, squared norm 3, and coordinate sum 1, so all lie at squared distance \(3-1/D\) from \(c_G=D^{-1}\mathbf1\). The degree-dependent weights are strictly positive, sum to one by the degree identity \(\sum_{e=\{u,v\}}(1/d_u+1/d_v)=|V|\), and give every vertex-coordinate and edge-coordinate of the barycenter exactly \(1/D\). The weighted parallel-axis identity then gives \(\max_p\|p-q\|^2\ge 3-1/D+\|q-c_G\|^2\) for every alternative center \(q\). This proves feasibility, optimality, uniqueness, and contact of all source vertices without any finite-enumeration assumption.

value.rationale: Cosmological polytopes are a canonical graph-to-polytope construction with an active literature on faces, triangulations, Ehrhart theory, and positive geometry. The theorem reveals a graph-independent Euclidean invariant across the entire connected family: once the ambient affine dimension parameter \(D=|V|+|E|\) is fixed, every incidence pattern has exactly the same circumradius. The explicit degree-weighted contact certificate explains why highly irregular graphs still share the same minimum enclosing sphere and gives a reusable geometric identity rather than a finite table or a single special graph computation.
